Instantiating Applications quickly
• 	When launching a full stack (EC2, EBS, RDS), it can take time to:
• 	Install applications
• 	Insert initial (or recovery) data

• 	We can take advantage of the cloud to speed that up!

Instantiating Applications quickly
• 	EC2 Instances:
• 	Use a Golden AMI: Install your applications, OS dependencies etc.. beforehand
and launch your EC2 instance from the Golden AMI
• 	Bootstrap using User Data: For dynamic configuration, use User Data scripts
• 	Hybrid: mix Golden AMI and User Data (Elastic Beanstalk)
• 	RDS Databases:
• 	Restore from a snapshot: the database will have schemas and data ready!
• 	EBS Volumes:
• 	Restore from a snapshot: the disk will already be formatted and have data!

content.summary:
## Making a web tier truly stateless

Store session data in an appropriate external shared store or use carefully designed client-side sessions. Then any healthy web instance can handle a request without recovering local process state.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

The infrastructure can replace failed compute only if application state survives elsewhere. Stickiness does not preserve a failed server, and concentrating instances in one AZ reduces resilience rather than fixing session persistence.

### Avoid this trap

Sticky sessions can improve locality but do not protect session state when an instance fails. Shared storage and security constraints must be considered explicitly.

### Apply it

Users are logged out whenever a web server is replaced. The fleet already uses a multi-AZ ALB and Auto Scaling. What is the most durable correction?

**Recommended design:** Externalize session state and make the web instances replaceable.

The infrastructure can replace failed compute only if application state survives elsewhere. Stickiness does not preserve a failed server, and concentrating instances in one AZ reduces resilience rather than fixing session persistence.

content.supplement: Tutor-authored explanation using architectural knowledge alongside the cited main-source chapter. These are original practice questions, not official AWS exam questions. Supplementary reading is listed separately; vocabulary overlap does not establish factual agreement.

cards.question: What allows any healthy web instance to handle a session?
cards.answer: Session state stored outside the individual instance.

cards.question: Do sticky sessions preserve state after instance failure?
cards.answer: No. They only influence request routing.

quiz.question: Users are logged out whenever a web server is replaced. The fleet already uses a multi-AZ ALB and Auto Scaling. What is the most durable correction?
options: Enable stickiness and continue keeping the only session copy in process memory.
Move all instances into one AZ so users stay close to the session server.
Externalize session state and make the web instances replaceable.
Disable health checks so failed instances are not removed.
quiz.explanation: The infrastructure can replace failed compute only if application state survives elsewhere. Stickiness does not preserve a failed server, and concentrating instances in one AZ reduces resilience rather than fixing session persistence.

content.summary:
## Decoupling slow work from request handling

Accept the request, persist a job to a durable queue and let independent workers process it. Track job state and make retries idempotent so duplicate deliveries do not duplicate business effects.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

A durable queue separates request acceptance from processing speed and supports independent scaling. Long synchronous requests consume web capacity. Workers need visibility-timeout, retry, duplicate handling and failure policies that match the job duration.

### Avoid this trap

A queue does not create unlimited processing capacity or guarantee exactly-once business operations. Monitor age and backlog and use dead-letter handling for poison messages.

### Apply it

Image conversion takes several minutes and demand arrives in bursts. The web tier must respond quickly even during a spike. Which design is most appropriate?

**Recommended design:** Queue conversion jobs and scale independent workers using backlog-related metrics.

cards.question: How can a web API hand off a slow background job?
cards.answer: Persist a job to a durable queue for independent workers.

cards.question: Why should queue workers be idempotent?
cards.answer: Retries or duplicate deliveries must not duplicate business effects.

quiz.question: Image conversion takes several minutes and demand arrives in bursts. The web tier must respond quickly even during a spike. Which design is most appropriate?
options: Increase every HTTP timeout and run conversion synchronously on the web servers.
Store pending jobs only in the load balancer memory.
Use DNS TTL changes to schedule individual conversion tasks.
Queue conversion jobs and scale independent workers using backlog-related metrics.
